text:
maria: FYI pushed a new dashboard panel for cold->warm transition today, noticing a weird dip in token-saved after the kernel-fold change. screenshot: https://ourdash/reports/ccw-1705 :eyes:
anya: saw that — looks like per-route there's a spike in cache misses right after the first 2s of a session. metrics: miss_rate +12% for model-rw-13B on /generate
devon: timeline? did this start around the kernel selection tweak we rolled last night?
maria: yes, rollout started at 1704988800 UTC (kernel fold v2). The panel annotates the rollout window.
raj: quick summary from profiling: batching heuristics now buffer longer for small requests, which increased kernel batch size but also changed KV eviction ordering in the runtime. I think some prefix keys are getting evicted before warmup prefetch completes.
anya: can you paste the profiler snippet that shows eviction ordering?
raj: sure, run this locally to replicate minimal repro:
```
./run_profiler --model model-rw-13B --sim-seqs 200 --kernel-fold v2 --prefetch true --log-evictions > ev.log
```
most runs show a repeated pattern: hot key enqueued, then a later micro-batch causes earlier KV segments to be freed because `kv_budget -= batch_memory` happens before `commit_prefetch`.
devon: ugh. that matches the traces I saw: KV cache misses for identical prompt tokens but different tenant IDs (same prompt content) — suggests key normalization/tenant scoping mismatch surface.
maria: per-customer breakdown (panel) shows Customer: acme-eng has 3.4x drop in token-saved vs baseline; others unaffected. acme uses short prompts and lots of small completions -> sensitive to micro-batching changes.
anya: could be two things then: (1) kernel batching reorder + prefetched keys race, (2) key fingerprinting changed with kernel v2 because we now include sequence-length bucket in key. Did we change key derivation?
raj: we accidentally included the `batch_bucket` field in key hash when merging kernel metadata. PR #7891. If batching heuristics vary between nodes, same input can map to different keys. That would explain customer-specific variance.
devon: that is a regression then. We should revert key derivation change immediately and patch kernel metadata handling.
maria: Agreed. Short-term mitigations on dashboard: add an annotation and a filter to exclude prefetch_missing spikes, and add alert rule: token-saved drop > 20% sustained for 10m for any tenant -> page on-call.
anya: I've created a temporary query to recompute normalized keys (treating `batch_bucket` as ignored) for the last 48h and re-evaluated hit-rate. SQL used: 
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, route, SUM(tokens_saved) as saved
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE event_time >= now() - interval '48 hours'
AND key_hash = sha256(concat(prompt_fingerprint, tenant_id, model))
GROUP BY tenant_id, route
ORDER BY saved DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
this recomputed baseline brings acme-eng back to expected saved range.
raj: action items: (1) revert PR #7891 in kernel meta merge (ETA 30m), (2) run prefetch reingest job for affected window (1704984000-1704996000) with normalized keys (ETA 2h), (3) add unit test to ensure key derivation invariant (ETA next sprint).
maria: I'll update the dashboard panels to show both `raw_key_hitrate` and `normalized_key_hitrate` side-by-side so we can validate reingest effect.
devon: please also add a small synthetic workload to smoke test per-tenant behaviors post-revert. Something like:
```bash
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s http://localhost:8080/generate -s scripts/short-prompt.lua
```
should exercise the micro-batching path.
anya: pinging @eng-oncall after we roll the revert; want to make sure alerting thresholds are tuned before we re-ingest to avoid pages.
obs-bot: Dashboard panel "cold->warm token-saved" updated by maria at 1705000060.
maria: rolled back PR in canary at 1705000100, canary metrics show hit-rate recovering, token-saved trending up. Will coordinate reingest once canary is stable for 10m.
raj: copying the kernel log snippet that showed mismatch for a single prompt across two nodes (nodeA vs nodeB):
```
nodeA: key_hash=0x9a3f... meta={model:rw-13B, batch_bucket:small}
nodeB: key_hash=0x4b12... meta={model:rw-13B, batch_bucket:medium}
```
same prompt_fingerprint, different hash -> duplicate entries and lower reuse.
devon: great catch. After reingest we should see consolidated hits and token-saved delta recover.
maria: I'll leave the dashboard annotation and keep the temporary normalized-key panel for 24h. If recovery looks good after reingest, we'll close this thread. :thumbsup:
anya: leaving a note to add an observability test: simulate divergent batch_bucket values and assert normalized grouping recovers the cache hit.
raj: thanks all — tracking in backlog as KER-447.
maria: resolving for now, will post another update after the full reingest (ETA ~2h).
